title: Evaluation metrics
task_statement: Define a primary metric, guard metrics, and thresholds before you tune a Claude system. (Inference: wording from secondary sources)

components.name: Success criteria and primary metric
components.first_principle: A metric measures the goal only when it names the goal and a threshold before tuning starts.
steps: Write each success criterion as a specific and measurable statement.
Set a threshold for each criterion on a held-out test set.
Name the primary metric from the criterion with the highest business impact. (Inference)
Add guard metrics for criteria that must not break. (Inference)
Assign one owner to each threshold before the first run. (Inference)
Run the same evaluation on each change and compare each score to its threshold.
pros: Turns vague quality goals into numbers that teams can compare.
Puts the most important criterion first in every report.
Gives the release decision a fixed bar.
cons: Measures only the criteria that someone wrote down.
Quantitative metrics can miss quality that people judge differently. (Inference)
Thresholds need review when the task mix changes. (Inference)
use_when: The application has a task outcome that code or a grader can check.
A team must decide whether a prompt or model change ships.
A stakeholder states a target for quality, cost, or response time.
do_not_use_when: The system is an early prototype with no users or decisions yet. (Inference)
No grader can measure the criterion, so the number would not mean anything. (Inference)
A single spot check serves a demo that has no decision attached. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Name one owner for each threshold in the evaluation plan. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Review each threshold when the task mix changes. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Assign a team member who can write rubrics and read score tables. (Inference)
Set an acceptable response time from the real-time needs of the application.
constraints.combination: Report time to first token separately for streaming responses.

constraints.choice: Set a budget per completed task, not per token.
constraints.combination: Track the same budget as a guard metric on each release. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Run the evaluation on every change to the prompt, model, or tools. (Inference)

components.exam_tie: D4.1. Expect a scenario where a proxy score looks good and the business outcome looks poor. The credited answer sets the business outcome as the primary metric with a threshold. (Inference)
components.trap: A fluency or length score that rises while task success stays flat. The score looks better, but it does not measure the goal.
components.decision_rule: Make the business outcome the primary metric, and keep proxy scores as diagnostics.
components.exam_tip: A metric with no threshold and no owner cannot decide a release.

key_facts.text: Good success criteria are specific, measurable, achievable, and relevant.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: The docs example sets an F1 score of at least 0.85 on a held-out test set of 10,000 posts.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Operational metrics include response time in milliseconds and uptime in percent.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Most use cases need multidimensional evaluation along several success criteria.
key_facts.label: Fact

components.name: Cost and latency metrics
components.first_principle: You pay for completed tasks, so cost per completed task measures value better than cost per token.
steps: Read the usage fields in each response to count input and output tokens.
Count the tasks that pass the primary metric.
Divide total spend by the count of completed tasks.
Pull daily organization totals from the Usage and Cost API.
Measure time to first token and baseline latency for streaming calls.
pros: Usage fields report token counts for every response.
The Usage and Cost API reports organization totals in USD by day.
Cost per completed task links spend to the goal.
cons: Usage and cost data can appear later than 5 minutes after a request.
The Cost API supports only daily buckets.
Claude Platform on AWS has no programmatic Usage and Cost endpoints.
use_when: Budget binds and the team compares models or prompts.
A team reports spend against completed outcomes.
A stakeholder sets a response time target for the application.
do_not_use_when: A minute-level view of cost is needed, because the Cost API has daily buckets only.
One response shows the cost of a single call, which is not a rate. (Inference)
Token counts alone decide the model choice, because the docs advise a per-task comparison.

constraints.choice: Track cost per completed task for each model and prompt version.
constraints.combination: Use the Usage and Cost API for daily totals in USD.

constraints.choice: Measure time to first token for streaming and baseline latency for other calls.
constraints.combination: Compare both with the response time target from the application.

constraints.choice: Poll the Usage API no more than once per minute for sustained use.
Use minute buckets for near-real-time views and daily buckets for reports.
Filter usage by workspace and API key to assign spend to owners.
constraints.combination: Call the endpoints with an Admin API credential, because workspace API keys do not work.

native_services.text: The programmatic Usage and Cost API endpoints are not currently available. Use the Usage and Cost pages in the Claude Console.

native_services.service: Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed)
native_services.text: Only the usage endpoint is available. Call it with Google Cloud credentials. The only predefined IAM role that allows the call is roles/claude.admin.

components.exam_tie: D4.1. Expect a scenario where a spend or latency target conflicts with a quality target. The credited answer measures cost per completed task against the quality threshold. (Inference)
components.trap: A lower price per token after a change. Fewer tasks may complete, so the cost per completed task can rise.
components.decision_rule: Report spend next to completed tasks and the quality threshold in the same view.
components.exam_tip: A cost figure without a completed-task count does not answer a cost question.

key_facts.text: The Usage API supports 1m, 1h, and 1d time buckets.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: The default limit for 1m buckets is 60, and the maximum is 1,440 buckets.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Usage and cost data typically appears within 5 minutes of request completion.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: The API supports polling once per minute for sustained use.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: The Cost API reports costs in USD and supports only daily buckets.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: The docs advise a comparison of models on cost per completed task, not on cost per token.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Time to first token matters most when you use streaming. Baseline latency measures the full response time.
key_facts.label: Fact

decision_flow:
flowchart TD
  A{Goal stated as a measurable outcome?} -->|No| B[Write success criteria with a threshold]
  A -->|Yes| C{Outcome is the primary metric?}
  C -->|No| D[Demote the proxy to a diagnostic]
  C -->|Yes| E{Safety or cost floor at stake?}
  E -->|Yes| F[Add guard metrics with a threshold]
  E -->|No| G[Keep one primary metric and track the rest]
cheatsheet:
flowchart LR
  G[Business goal] --> P[Primary metric]
  P --> T[Threshold]
  T --> O[Owner]
  P --> R1[Guard: safety at zero]
  P --> R2[Guard: latency target]
  P --> R3[Guard: cost per completed task]
  X[Proxy metric] --> D[Diagnostic only]

patterns.wording: a proxy score rises while the business outcome stays flat
patterns.answer_type: primary metric on the business outcome
patterns.rule: Make the outcome the primary metric with a threshold. Keep the proxy as a diagnostic.
traps: Move to a larger model tier before the measurement

patterns.wording: the team needs a number for a vague quality goal
patterns.answer_type: criterion with a threshold and an owner
patterns.rule: Turn the goal into a measurable criterion, then attach a threshold and an owner.
traps: Add more logging with no threshold

patterns.wording: spend rises after a change that adds more tasks to the queue
patterns.rule: Divide spend by completed tasks and compare that value across versions.
traps: Cut tokens without a check of the quality threshold
